summary: The flagship Javelin coder: a ~72B-parameter open base, adapted with Javelin's tool-calling and verify/repair policy. This is a declared target — it is NOT trained or served until real weights exist.

base.note: There is no open 80B coder today, so '80B class' is served by the real 72B open base. The display name is the product name; this field is the truth about what is actually underneath.

requirements.trainNote: QLoRA fine-tuning of a 72B base needs roughly 80GB of VRAM (one H100/A100-80GB) or multi-GPU sharding. It does not fit consumer hardware.
requirements.mergeNote: Merging the adapter back into full bf16 weights needs ~160GB, so it is done on a rented multi-GPU host, not locally.
requirements.serveNote: Serving is possible in 4-bit on a single 48GB card, or across two 24GB cards. A quantized GGUF can run on far less, slower.

training.note: A model this size is only worth training on a large, high-quality, human-reviewed dataset. Promoting a small synthetic set to 72B wastes the compute.

rented.detail: Recommended: a single H100 80GB (or 2xA100-80GB for the merge) for a few hours on RunPod/Lambda/CoreWeave. This is the only realistic route.

local.detail: Not trainable on consumer GPUs. A 16GB or 24GB card cannot hold the base, the optimizer state, or the activations.

cpu.detail: Not feasible. CPU LoRA works up to ~1.5B; a 72B base is many orders of magnitude beyond it.

status.note: Set trained/served true ONLY by the pipeline when a verified adapter and served weights actually exist. Never edit these by hand to claim a model that was not built.
